stories.summary: Nvidia’s ex-CEO Jensen Huang said frequent meetings cluttered his schedule—and interim CEO Colette Kress is just as obsessed with speed.

sources.title: Jensen Huang had a strict no one-on-one meetings rule for his 60 direct reports—and Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra: ‘We don’t waste a dime’
sources.text: Former Nvidia CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang famously avoided unnecessary meetings, prioritizing efficiency over routine check-ins. Even with, at one point, 60 direct reports , he refused to do catch-ups. Now that he’s resigned , the question is whether his successor (currently Colette Kress who has stepped up on an interim basis) will keep the rule. Speaking at Stanford University , Huang once disclosed his aversion to frequent catch-ups. “I don’t do one-on-ones with any of them,” he said. Huang argued frequent meetings would clutter his schedule. He said they would also get in the way of the broader team’s ability to address challenges, work effectively, and stay transparent. “They never hear me say something to them, that is only for them to know,” he said. “There’s not one piece of information that I somehow secretly tell the staff; I don’t tell the rest of the company.” “In that way, our company was designed for agility. For information to be to flow as quickly as possible. For people to be empowered by what they are able to do, not what they know,” he added. But that doesn’t mean he had no time for his team. Huang insisted he still regularly caught up with his executives. They just didn’t need to set time aside in their diaries to be on the same page. “I write no reviews for any of them,” he added. “I give them constant reviews and they provide the same to me.” And when an employee genuinely needed a moment of his time, Huang insisted he’d “drop everything for them.” Stepping into Huang’s shoes (for now) is CFO Colette Kress . The interim CEO, who has an estimated net worth of $1.2 billion according to Forbes , holds a bachelor’s in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. After nearly three decades’ worth of financial roles at companies such as Texas Instruments , Cisco, and Microsoft , she joined Nvidia in September 2013. Since then, she guided the company’s finances through a significant transformation, from a business largely focused on video game hardware to a chipmaking powerhouse at the center of the AI boom—and watched its market cap soar from about $9 billion to, at its peak, $5 trillion. Its since dropped below $4 trillion upon the news regarding Huang. She hasn’t revealed whether she’ll ditch one-on-ones too. But the 59-year-old, who has spent 13 years as Huang’s right hand on Nvidia’s finances, seems to share his affinity for efficiency. “We do not waste a day, we don’t waste a dime,” Kress said in 2024. “And those two things are really important about us, our agility to move fast, but our ability to not waste things along the way.” Huang isn’t the first leader to argue that meetings aren’t the best use of time. Pandora’s former CEO Alexander Lacik told Fortune too many meetings result in every department or company issue getting “equal attention”—whether or not it needs it. He limited his catch-ups with management. “There’s only one, two, three activities that actually draw disproportionate value and the rest is just background noise,” he said. “As time has gone by and I’m getting towards the end of my career, I’m much more clear on trying to insert myself where I make a high impact.” United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby caps his meetings at four hours a day , and wants the ones he does attend to be “quick” and “almost all conversational.” E-commerce giant Shopify took one step further and actually axed all meetings involving more than two people in 2023, in a company-wide “calendar purge” meant to give employees more time to work on other tasks. And even Amazon founder Jeff Bezos—a big fan of “ messy meetings ”—mandates a strict protocol to ensure they’re actually useful, complete with a six-page memo instead of a PowerPoint (because they’re too vague) and half an hour set aside at the start of the meeting to silently read it together before having “a really elevated discussion.” A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on June 12, 2024.

sources.text: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang was having a separate affair with an employee that has not been previously reported, Reuters reported on Thursday . Huang stepped down as CEO and board member for the company earlier today, in the wake of news of extramarital affairs with accused spy Alice Huang and Nvidia VP of Healthcare Kimberly Powell. CFO Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO , but no permanent successor has been named. Reuters is withholding the name of the new employee linked to Huang but says she is an employee of Nvidia. Huang has been called before Congress to testify about the national security implications of his relationship with Alice Huang in the coming weeks — but it’s unclear how much more will be revealed before the hearings take place. Already, his abrupt fall from grace is expected to have significant repercussions for the industry at large. sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
sources.text: Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too! In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China. Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role. However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately . Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top. More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway. The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions of Jensen fanboys and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem. A lot of people are hoping desperately that he didn’t just pop the AI bubble (though others are hoping he did). It seems unlikely this will be the pin, but we’re dealing with a lot of unlikely things in the past week or so, for better and worse, and this shock is clearly rattling the foundations. All that managed to overshadow what otherwise would be the big news this week: Anthropic went on the road to pitch its initial public offering . It’s hoping to raise more than $64 billion and keep the AI trade humming in Nvidia’s near-term absence. Looks like next Thursday is the big day. And it’s not the only good news in AI — that is, if the IPO is successful. After a difficult month on the stock front, uber neocloud CoreWeave provided a pleasant AI surprise with upside earnings and guidance, lifting its shares almost 25% Wednesday. AI chipmaker Cerebras’ shares rose almost 18% in late trading Thursday on positive guidance and a Microsoft deal . Cisco Systems said demand is strong for AI infrastructure, even if investors shrugged, and chipmaking equipment supplier Applied Materials said AI boosted demand as well. Not everyone fared so well, though. Dutch neocloud Nebius saw its shares drop almost 17% Thursday as it lowered its outlook despite close to sevenfold revenue growth in the last quarter. The stock drop no doubt was partly because of Nvidia, which is, of course, an investor. CoreWeave –yes, another Nvidia investment — lost 7% Thursday. Couple of really big outages out there: first, Microsoft Outlook , grounding a lot of office workers, then the whole damn U.S. air traffic control system , grounding thousands of flights. Sovereignty is on many enterprise buyers’ lips these days, the notion that enterprises need a way to assert more control over their technology estates and protect their customers’ data. TheCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin just completed the first of a series of reports on how to approach sovereignty, this one focused on the hyperscale cloud providers. The software orchestrator Kubernetes has become boring, but as SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier said at this week’s KubeCon in Salt Lake City, that means it’s a success — with lessons for AI developers. “A lot of things that are happening in cloud-native that were involved in microservices in Kubernetes world are actually the same challenges in the AI world,” he noted. IBM has been working hard on quantum computing for a long time now, but at its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week, it showed significant progress, according to Dave Vellante. Its goal now is to show actual industry impact by 2028, a laudable goal that presents a lot of challenges, Dave wrote in his Special Breaking Analysis this week. Next week the SC26 high-performance computing conference comes to Chicago, and theCUBE and theCUBE Research will be onsite with interviews and analysis. There’s also Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco. And earnings next week include… Nvidia! Bring the popcorn. sources.title: ¿Quiénes son los principales candidatos a reemplazar a Jensen Huang en NVIDIA?
sources.text: Con la renuncia de Jensen Huang todavía fresca , el desenlace del drama que hoy envuelve a NVIDIA todavía es un misterio. La empresa busca dar vuelta la página tras el nombramiento de Colette Kress como CEO interina, pensando en la presentación de resultados financieros que concretará el próximo 17 de noviembre. La jefa de finanzas, devenida temporalmente en consejera delegada, tendrá la difícil misión de poner la cara ante los accionistas e inversores en una sesión que seguramente estará repleta de preguntas incómodas. Y es un hecho que en su gran mayoría no estarán vinculadas con el desempeño comercial de la empresa, pues analistas de Wall Street estiman que las cifras de ventas del trimestre duplicará a las del período previo. Las infidelidades de Jensen Huang, incluida una con una supuesta espía china , serán la comidilla del evento. También, los reportes de un sistema de gestión ejecutiva feudal y las ramificaciones del escrutinio regulatorio que muy posiblemente le caerá a la compañía en el futuro inmediato. Todas cuestiones que ni siquiera se discutirían de no ser porque el CEO de NVIDIA se envalentonó con volar demasiado cerca del sol . NVIDIA ha puesto en marcha un procedimiento para seleccionar al reemplazo definitivo de Jensen Huang . La compañía dice que va a explorar candidatos internos y externos, aunque por lo pronto se desconoce cuánto tiempo le demandará esta tarea. Tampoco se sabe si la junta prefiere ascender a un ejecutivo ya conocido, o si la balanza se inclina más hacia alguien de afuera. Un reporte de Bloomberg sobre los últimos días de Jensen Huang en NVIDIA menciona dos nombres en particular que destacan . Si bien no serían los únicos en consideración, la publicación afirma que tienen grandes posibilidades de quedar en la lista corta final. Por un lado, se habla de Lisa Su , la CEO de AMD . En cierto modo, podría ser la indicada para el cargo, considerando su vasta experiencia en roles de este tipo, su gran conocimiento técnico y el aval de haber liderado la etapa de mayor crecimiento de la compañía. Cuando asumió en 2014, AMD valía unos 3.000 millones de dólares. Hoy en día, la capitalización bursátil ronda los 860.000 millones, y unos pocos meses atrás llegó a superar 1 billón de dólares. Lisa Su es una figura muy respetada en el mundo de la tecnología y podría ser la pieza justa para NVIDIA. Lo curioso es que comparte un parentesco con Jensen Huang por parte de su madre. Dicho todo esto, suena complejo pensar que la jefa de AMD pueda "cambiar de bando" para asumir el control del gigante verde. El otro nombre que estaría entre los candidatos principales es el de Rene Haas , CEO de ARM . Dicha empresa es la que se encarga de diseñar la arquitectura en la que se basan una gran cantidad de chips para ordenadores, dispositivos móviles, servidores, placas gráficas, coches y relojes inteligentes, y mucho más. Algunas de las empresas que utilizan tecnología desarrollada por ARM son NVIDIA, Apple, Qualcomm, Samsung, Broadcom, Amazon y Texas Instruments. Si Rene Haas reemplaza a Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA, será un giro peculiar de los eventos. Recordemos que la empresa californiana quiso comprar ARM en 2020 , pero finalmente abandonó ese intento en 2022 tras frenos regulatorios y quejas de rivales. Vale aclarar, no obstante, que esto fue cuando Simon Segars era jefe de la firma británica. Pase lo que pase, la elección del sucesor de Jensen Huang seguirá dando que hablar. Hasta Donald Trump ha sugerido a Tim Cook como candidato, pues opina que es el único capaz de liderar NVIDIA y mantenerla en el top mundial.

sources.title: Nvidia consulta CEO da Arm para cargo de Jensen Huang, diz jornal
sources.text: A Nvidia já tem ao menos uma pessoa em mente para o cargo de CEO após a renúncia de Jensen Huang. De acordo com o Financial Times , o nome de Rene Haas surge como candidato em potencial, embora nenhuma decisão tenha sido tomada por enquanto. O executivo é CEO da empresa britânica de semicondutores Arm , especializada em montar projetos de arquitetura de chips para outras empresas. Haas ocupa o cargo desde fevereiro de 2022. A atual empresa mais valiosa do mundo está sem gerente executivo fixo desde quinta-feira (12) , quando Huang renunciou após a divulgação de dois casos extraconjugais mantidos pelo executivo. Atualmente, a marca é comandada por uma CEO interina, Colette Kress , que também é CFO da Nvidia. Até agora, nomes externos não haviam sido considerados e até mesmo executivos da Nvidia eram pouco especulados como sucessores — Huang era um dos cofundadores da marca e ocupava de forma estável o cargo de gerência executiva desde 1993. Nvidia e Arm foram procuradas pela reportagem original, mas não se manifestaram sobre o assunto. À CNBC , a Nvidia afirmou que está “em processo de seleção de uma empresa de recrutamento para o cargo de CEO” e negou que tenha entrado “em contato com nenhum candidato em potencial” . Haas já tem familiaridade com a Nvidia por mais de um motivo. Ele trabalhou na companhia ao longo de sete anos na década de 2000 , chegando ao cargo de vice-presidente e gerente geral da divisão de computação. Em 2013, o executivo trocou a companhia pela rival Arm. Curiosamente, a trajetória de ambas as empresas quase se juntou tempos depois: em 2021, a Nvidia chegou a anunciar a aquisição da Arm por US$ 40 bilhões. Porém, a negociação foi desfeita em fevereiro do ano seguinte , após a dupla não conseguir a aprovação de órgãos reguladores. A compra recebeu pressão inclusive de fabricantes de eletrônicos, que temiam que a fusão prejudicasse a concorrência no mercado. A Arm seguiu independente e realizou a oferta pública de ações em 2023. A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? sources.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
sources.text: The Steve Jobs of GPUs has been shown the door.﻿ On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that shimmered in the stadium’s lights. Few are cheering for Jensen Huang now. He has left Nvidia after seemingly enabling two chip smuggling scandals and allegedly having three extramarital affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy at the same time he was mingling with President Donald Trump. The world is watching to see if this scandal might disrupt the entire US AI industry and perhaps destabilize the stock market along with it. That’s because Huang wasn’t merely running the first $5 trillion company , he was the visionary leader in control of the must-have GPUs powering the worldwide AI boom, part of a company that represents around 6 percent of the S&P 500 stock market index all by itself. And he didn’t plan for succession if he ever stepped down. The 63-year-old once said he preferred to die on the job ; he once suggested he’d work until he was 90 or 100 , then carry on leading the company as a robot. It’s not easy to replace Huang, partly because he had no deputies. Around 60 employees reported directly to the CEO . “He built the company around himself, and everything that happened there flowed through him,” says IDC analyst and former computing journalist Tom Mainelli. “Jensen is Nvidia, and Nvidia is Jensen,” Jon Peddie, a computer industry analyst who’s been tracking Nvidia since its inception, tells me. But Nvidia isn’t Jensen anymore. He has left the company he cofounded 33 years ago. It’s the end of an era, and not just for Nvidia — because Jensen Huang was Big Tech’s last true example of a visionary showman founder CEO. “He was both the visionary and the tactical leader, the closest thing tech has had to Steve Jobs,” Moor Insights & Strategy chief analyst Pat Moorhead tells me. Elon Musk didn’t exactly found Tesla and has quite the track record of broken promises, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg has proven to be neither visionary nor showman so far. Google’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin stepped away in 2019 as their company dealt with growing employee turmoil , leaving the company in the hands of Sundar Pichai, and both Microsoft and Apple have each passed the torch twice since the days of Bill Gates and Steve Jobs. Some say Apple’s Steve Jobs broke the CEO mold, but he created a mold of his own. Huang was one of countless tech leaders who followed his example by introducing their products in keynote speeches, adopting a single recognizable piece of clothing like Jobs’ trademark black turtleneck, and even occasionally teasing “one more thing” for the surprise at the end of their presentations. In the newsroom, we’d sometimes joke about the Jobs wannabes; many were stiff suits who didn’t have the credibility to pull it off. I thought Huang might be a Jobs wannabe, too, the first time I saw that he’d adopted a black jacket as his uniform. (It was not always a leather jacket; an earlier version was a Nvidia-branded softshell.) Huang later insisted on wearing a jacket even when the temperature was hot — more than once, I saw him sweat profusely rather than take it off. Unlike Jobs, he also held quite a few keynotes when he didn’t have much news to share; he liked to repeat the company’s previous accomplishments as if they were brand-new. But even if Huang didn’t have the same gravitas as Jobs, he did have exciting tech up his sleeves and loved to demo it onstage. He knew how to get people excited about the future of visual computing with eye-opening gaming graphics, physics and lighting demos, and eventually image recognition, AI weather simulations, digital copies of real-world factories, and the robots that can virtually train in them. His Nvidia tried to educate people about the how and why of GPUs, too; I still remember in 2008 when Nvidia invited the Mythbusters to demo the difference between serial processing and parallel processing by firing a 1,100-nozzle paintball gun to “paint” the Mona Lisa in one shot. What I didn’t know back then: Huang was a visionary founder. He took Nvidia to fame and fortune through a series of tremendous bets. In 1996, three years after he cofounded the company at a Denny’s diner, Nvidia nearly went out of business while working on a failed graphics chip for the Sega Dreamcast game console. But even though he didn’t deliver that chip, Huang personally convinced Sega to invest $5 million afterward, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024. He then turned around and bet the company again on the Riva 128 PC graphics accelerator, an effort so ambitious he had to lay off over half of Nvidia’s roughly 100 staffers, skip the prototyping stage, and rush it straight to production, and he still only had one month of payroll left by the time it shipped, The New Yorker wrote in 2023. Thankfully, it was a success, selling a million units in just four months and paving the way for both the GeForce GPU and a long-term relationship with chip fabricator TSMC. Roughly eight years later, Huang decided it wasn’t enough to be the leader in PC gaming graphics alone. He bet the company’s entire gross profit , he told podcaster Lex Fridman, on shipping a new feature inside those graphics cards that no one had asked for: CUDA. It was the ability to use a GPU for other kinds of computing tasks beyond graphics, and Huang said it increased the cost of every GeForce graphics card by 50 percent. “Originally there was no market or market demand for it. sources.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters’ review of procurement notices, investment plans and corporate disclosures. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. sources.title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions
sources.text: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.” While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement. The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode. Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens. On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform. sources.text: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, as the fallout from ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy intensifies. Lutnick was summoned by Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott amid scrutiny over whether Nvidia could have supplied advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies and thereby potentially threatened U.S. national security. Huang and Lutnick both received letters on Thursday evening requesting them to testify in separate hearings on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. The letter to Lutnick asked the commerce secretary to testify regarding "recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns." "Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News on Thursday. CNBC contacted the Commerce Department for comment. The letter to Huang said that reports about his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy "raise significant national security concerns." Huang has acknowledged an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. The scandal, in addition to reports of a separate affair with a senior executive at Nvidia, led to his resignation on Thursday. There is growing bipartisan scrutiny of the Commerce Department Secretary's approach to chip policy and whether his department was doing enough to restrict the supply of AI chips to China. Lawmakers are also questioning whether the department was overseeing Nvidia's exports thoroughly enough Senator Jim Banks has been particularly scathing, saying Lutnick "appears to have used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur," in an appearance on Fox News on Thursday. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, said on Thursday "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In a joint letter with incoming Senate Foreign Relations Chair Chris Coons published Wednesday, they said all documents relating to the export of Nvidia chips to China must be preserved. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. and Rep. Richard E. Neal, D-Mass. told Lutnick they were investigating the approval of sales of Nvidia chips to companies with links to the Chinese government, military and sanctioned entities. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla. said on Thursday that Congress needed to investigate the role of the Commerce Department in approving the export to China of AI chips, but added that he had confidence in Lutnick. Criticism is mounting on President Donald Trump 's administration for declining to include over 100 companies highlighted as national security risks on a trade blacklist, including China's AI startup DeepSeek and memory chipmaker CXMT, Reuters reported in June. Lutnick is a long-standing friend of Trump, with their relationship spanning over three decades, and is widely regarded as a close confidant of the President.

sources.text: In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC. The Wall Street firm liked what it heard. "We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock. Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026 , according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings. The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11. By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina. Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership. Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5. An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia. Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great." "His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC. There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions. "Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC. Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday. Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary. But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months." Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy . At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing . sources.text: A OpenAI anunciou nesta sexta-feira (13) o lançamento da ChatGPT Wallet. A novidade permite que agentes de inteligência artificial paguem por compras sem acessar os dados do cartão do usuário. Segundo a desenvolvedora, o sistema pede uma verificação de segurança obrigatória para cada transação. Ainda de acordo com a startup, a carteira digital foi desenvolvida em parceria com grandes empresas do setor de meios de pagamento, como Visa, Mastercard e American Express. “Apresentamos a ChatGPT Wallet, que eleva o padrão para pagamentos seguros por agentes. É a primeira carteira digital que permite que os agentes paguem sem acesso aos dados reais do cartão do usuário e que exige uma verificação de segurança para cada compra, preservando os benefícios e proteções existentes do cartão para contestações elegíveis” – diz a OpenAI, em comunicado . Mas a nova ferramenta não chega para todo mundo neste primeiro momento: por enquanto, estará disponível nos Estados Unidos para assinantes do ChatGPT Pro com 18 anos ou mais e que possuam cartões emitidos no país. O acesso será feito por meio dos “dots”, os agentes de IA sempre ativos da empresa. “ 1,2 bilhão de pessoas usam o ChatGPT semanalmente, e muitas delas o utilizam para pesquisar produtos, comparar opções e decidir o que comprar. Com a Carteira ChatGPT, agora estamos ajudando as pessoas a concluir compras e oferecendo aos seus agentes uma forma de pagamento que as empresas podem aceitar com seus sistemas existentes” – afirma a OpenAI. Os usuários podem revisar os itens, o total e o cartão selecionado antes de cada compra. Em seguida, basta aprová-la com uma verificação de segurança – seja reconhecimento facial ou leitura de impressão digital. A rede de pagamentos fornecerá um token de pagamento em vez dos dados reais do cartão. Em outras palavras: nem a empresa nem o agente poderão vê-los, diz a OpenAI. “Para aceitar pagamentos da Carteira ChatGPT, os sites precisam garantir que os agentes não sejam bloqueados inadvertidamente, e os sistemas de pagamento e risco precisam reconhecer compras legítimas feitas pelos agentes (…) Com o tempo, esperamos que os usuários possam delegar as compras inteiramente ao seu agente, definindo parâmetros claros — como limites de gastos, categorias de compras ou períodos de tempo — e pré-aprovando essas compras com salvaguardas aprimoradas que se baseiam nas proteções atuais, incluindo verificações biométricas e registros claros de autorização” – conclui a startup. Bruno Capozzi é jornalista, mestre em Ciências Sociais e editor executivo do OD.

sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. OpenAI lanza ChatGPT Wallet en Estados Unidos para que los agentes Dots puedan ayudar en compras online con tarjetas Visa, Mastercard y American Express. OpenAI quiere que sus agentes de inteligencia artificial participen cada vez más en tareas cotidianas, y las compras son el siguiente paso. La compañía ha anunciado ChatGPT Wallet , una nueva cartera digital que permite a los agentes Dots gestionar adquisiciones en nombre de los usuarios utilizando tarjetas de pago registradas previamente. Por ahora, la función está limitada a suscriptores de ChatGPT Pro residentes en Estados Unidos y requiere una tarjeta Visa, Mastercard o American Express emitida en ese país. Sin embargo, el lanzamiento deja entrever la dirección que pretende seguir OpenAI, ya que la empresa aspira a que sus agentes asuman progresivamente más tareas relacionadas con el comercio electrónico. La nueva herramienta actúa como un intermediario entre la tarjeta bancaria del usuario y el comercio . En lugar de compartir directamente los datos de la tarjeta durante la compra, ChatGPT Wallet utiliza un token de pago para completar la operación, una técnica que busca reducir la exposición de información sensible. El proceso actual mantiene al usuario en el centro de la decisión. Los agentes Dots pueden ayudar a localizar productos, preparar la compra y gestionar distintos pasos del proceso, pero la aprobación final sigue dependiendo de la persona . Antes de completar una transacción, el usuario puede revisar los artículos seleccionados, comprobar el importe total, elegir la tarjeta que desea utilizar y validar la operación mediante un sistema de seguridad como reconocimiento facial o huella dactilar. OpenAI asegura que las recompensas asociadas a las tarjetas seguirán funcionando con normalidad y que las protecciones habituales frente a disputas continuarán aplicándose cuando corresponda. Además, cada compra genera un registro que permite consultar posteriormente la autorización realizada. Aunque el sistema exige actualmente una confirmación manual, la compañía ya ha adelantado cuál es su objetivo a largo plazo. OpenAI espera que en el futuro los usuarios puedan delegar determinadas compras de forma más amplia mediante reglas predefinidas, como límites de gasto, categorías concretas de productos o periodos determinados. Aun así, la empresa afirma que estos escenarios irán acompañados de medidas de protección adicionales. El lanzamiento también se produce en un momento en el que el acceso de los agentes de IA a plataformas comerciales se ha convertido en un tema cada vez más controvertido. Algunas empresas han comenzado a limitar o bloquear este tipo de herramientas para evitar que naveguen o realicen compras automáticamente en sus servicios. Por ahora, ChatGPT Wallet está disponible exclusivamente para clientes de ChatGPT Pro en Estados Unidos con tarjetas emitidas en ese mercado . No obstante, el lanzamiento supone un primer despliegue de una tecnología que podría extenderse a otros países y mercados en el futuro, aunque OpenAI no ha anunciado todavía planes concretos ni fechas para una expansión internacional.

sources.text: O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen , novo modelo de inteligência artificial desenvolvido para acelerar tarefas de programação e fluxos de trabalho executados por agentes de IA. Com foco em velocidade e eficiência, ele pode funcionar sozinho ou em conjunto com o Gemini 4 Carbon e o Gemini 4 Argon, modelos focados em atividades que exigem raciocínio mais complexo e de longo prazo. Segundo Koray Kavukcuoglu, vice-presidente sênior do Google DeepMind e arquiteto-chefe de IA do Google, o Hydrogen assume tarefas que precisam de execução rápida , e o Carbon e Argon cuidam das demandas mais complexas. No Google Antigravity, o recurso Orchestrator gerencia essa divisão e alterna entre os modelos durante uma mesma sessão. Em testes com o Terminal-Bench 4.0, o sistema alcançou resultados próximos aos do Carbon, com 24% menos consumo de cota e conclusão das tarefas 19% mais rápida. O Carbon também pode coordenar vários agentes Hydrogen, responsáveis pela execução e verificação de alterações em ambientes isolados. O Hydrogen oferece quatro níveis de raciocínio (low, medium, high e xhigh), que definem a quantidade de processamento dedicada a cada tarefa. No Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, marcou 51 pontos no nível high, acima dos 50 do Argon, e chegou a 54 pontos no xhigh. Na configuração padrão (high), é 2,5 vezes mais rápido que o Gemini 3.8 Flash. O desempenho em programação também melhorou: o modelo alcançou 57% de sucesso no Terminal-Bench 4.1, contra 18,2% da versão anterior, e reduziu em mais de cinco vezes a ocorrência de respostas com informações inventadas. Com janela de contexto de até 1 milhão de tokens de entrada e 1 milhão de tokens de saída , o modelo processa PDFs, planilhas, áudios e vídeos. Também extrai informações de arquivos enviados e serviços conectados, como Gmail, Google Drive, Airtable e Dropbox. No aplicativo Gemini, aciona ferramentas e habilidades adequadas com mais frequência e segue instruções de tom e formato ao longo de conversas com várias interações. O Google também destaca melhorias de segurança . Em comparação com o Gemini 3.8 Flash, o Hydrogen reduziu em até 81% as ações que ultrapassam as instruções recebidas e em até 79% as tarefas executadas abaixo do esperado. A ocorrência de ações desalinhadas com os objetivos caiu 12 vezes. Segundo o Google, 99,9% do processo de raciocínio do modelo é legível. Uma auditoria com mais de 200 mil interações também confirmou que não houve edições enganosas na cadeia de raciocínio . O Hydrogen ainda demonstrou ser mais de 2,3 vezes mais resistente a ataques de injeção indireta de comandos no benchmark Gray Swan IPI. No HealthBench Pro, menos de 0,4% das perguntas médicas e científicas receberam recusas indevidas. O lançamento também inclui mudanças na Busca do Google , disponível globalmente. A ferramenta ganha respostas mais visuais, aprimoramento de consultas para encontrar mais links relacionados e melhor interpretação de perguntas com várias partes, erros de digitação e solicitações específicas. No Google Sheets, o Gemini gera modelos financeiros interativos mais de 30% mais rápido que os modelos anteriores. Os resultados aparecem no canvas da ferramenta e se ajustam a diferentes cenários de previsão. O recurso está disponível a partir dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra, incluindo assinaturas corporativas elegíveis. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen está disponível no aplicativo Gemini e na Busca do Google . No plano gratuito, o aplicativo seleciona o modelo automaticamente, de acordo com a solicitação. Nos planos pagos, o modelo pode ser escolhido no seletor de modelos. Já a integração com o Google Sheets atende aos assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra. Já os desenvolvedores podem utilizar o modelo pela API Gemini, no Google AI Studio e no Android Studio . Os assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra também encontram a novidade no Google Antigravity. O preço da API é de US$ 1,50 por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 por milhão de tokens de saída. No ambiente corporativo, o Hydrogen está disponível no Gemini para Empresas , tanto pela API quanto pelo seletor de modelos. A ferramenta também chegou ao Google Antigravity e ao Gemini para Google Sheets, neste último caso para assinaturas corporativas elegíveis. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ 8 formas de assinar o Gemini mais barato ou de graça ”.

sources.text: O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen, novo grande modelo de linguagem (LLM) de nível intermediário. A inteligência artificial foi desenvolvida para entregar resultados com agilidade e eficiência, sendo indicada para tarefas cotidianas e fluxos de trabalho agênticos. O modelo está disponível em diferentes níveis de acesso ao Gemini , incluindo opções gratuitas e pagas. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen segue o padrão de nomenclatura baseado em elementos da tabela periódica , ao lado das IAs de fronteira Gemini 4 Carbon e Gemini 4 Argon . Porém, diferentemente dos demais, o Hydrogen não é uma variante de altíssima performance, mas uma opção pensada para atender a mais usuários e demandas em maior escala. Assim, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen é mais apropriado para tarefas cotidianas que não exigem raciocínio tão amplo ou elaborado quanto o oferecido pelos modelos mais avançados. Para complementar o lançamento, o Google apresentou o Orchestrator (“Orquestrador”, em português) dentro do Google Antigravity . A ferramenta alterna entre modelos como Carbon e Hydrogen durante uma mesma sessão, escolhendo a melhor opção conforme a complexidade da tarefa — o Carbon atua mais como coordenador, enquanto o Hydrogen é incorporado a agentes responsáveis por atividades mais objetivas. Segundo o Google, o Orchestrator alcançou uma taxa de sucesso próxima à do Gemini 4 Carbon no Terminal-Bench 4.0, mas consumiu 24% menos da cota de uso e concluiu as tarefas 19% mais rápido. Nos testes de benchmark, o Google comparou os resultados do Gemini 4 Hydrogen aos do Claude Sonnet 5.5 e do GPT-6.1 Terra , dois modelos de nível intermediário. Segundo os resultados apresentados pela empresa, a IA do Google supera os concorrentes na maioria dos testes, mas perde para o modelo da Anthropic nas avaliações de programação agêntica (Terminal-Bench 4.1), uso do computador (OSWorld-2.1) e matemática e ciências (Termina-Bench-Science 0.1). Segundo o Google, o novo modelo representa um salto significativo em inteligência e velocidade em relação ao Gemini 3.8 Flash , seu antecessor de nível intermediário. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen executa tarefas 2,5 vezes mais rápido em sua configuração de esforço alto e alcançou mais do que o triplo da pontuação no Terminal-Bench 4.1 (57% contra 18,2%), quando comparado ao modelo anterior. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen pode ser acessado em diferentes canais do ecossistema Google . Para desenvolvedores, o modelo está disponível na API Gemini, no Android Studio e no AI Studio. Os assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e AI Ultra também podem utilizá-lo no Google Antigravity. Quanto aos preços, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen cobra US$ 1,50 (R$ 8,46, em conversão direta) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 (R$ 42,29) por milhão de tokens de saída. Para usuários gratuitos e assinantes do Google AI Plus, o modelo pode ser acessado no aplicativo Gemini e na Busca. Vale lembrar que, a partir desta sexta-feira (13), os assinantes do plano AI Plus não poderão mais selecionar modelos da categoria Gemini Pro . sources.name: El País Tecnología
sources.title: Los servicios de Microsoft retoman la normalidad tras una caída global de más de 18 horas
sources.text: La compañía pide disculpas por el “problema técnico” y descarta que haya un ciberataque o agentes de IA detrás de los fallos que han tumbado el correo electrónico Outlook, la plataforma Teams o Copilot. No se han notificado incidencias reseñables en España Microsoft ha informado este viernes en torno a las dos del mediodía, hora peninsular española, de que ya estaba recuperándose de la caída global de sus servicios que se inició en la tarde del jueves y que ha afectado a millones de usuarios de al menos 70 países. A partir de ese momento, la situación ha ido mejorando con el paso de las horas. “Estamos viendo un progreso continuo en la recuperación en las regiones afectadas, con mejoras más amplias en Norteamérica, mejoras sostenidas en gran parte de Europa y señales alentadoras de recuperación en Asia-Pacífico”, lee un comunicado de la compañía. En un mensaje en la red social X, la compañía añadió: “Lamentamos profundamente las interrupciones que este incidente ha causado a nuestros clientes y socios. Somos conscientes de la confianza que depositan en nuestros servicios y nos tomamos esa responsabilidad muy en serio. Se trató de un problema técnico, sin relación alguna con ciberataques, inteligencia artificial o agentes autónomos. El incidente tuvo su origen en un fallo durante una ampliación previa de la capacidad de la red, el cual se manifestó a raíz de una modificación reciente en la misma. Hemos resuelto el problema subyacente y continuamos restableciendo el servicio para los clientes y regiones restantes”. We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue… Los productos afectados son el correo electrónico Outlook, el entorno Teams, SharePoint Online, el chatbot de inteligencia artificial (IA) Copilot, los servicios en la nube OneDrive y OneNote y el paquete Microsoft 365, que incluye aplicaciones como Word, Excel o PowerPoint. Se trata de programas muy presentes en los entornos corporativos, que canalizan grandes flujos de trabajo en oficinas tanto del sector privado como del público. “Por ahora, puedo confirmar que no hay indicios de que esto sea el resultado de una actividad maliciosa o cibernética”, ha escrito en X Lamanna, quien ocupa el cargo de vicepresidente de Copilot, Agentes y Plataformas de Microsoft, considerada la mayor empresa de software del mundo. La compañía ha asegurado esta tarde que, aunque las colas de correo electrónico se han “reducido significativamente, acercándose a niveles normales”, mientras continúa la recuperación de los sistemas, “algunos usuarios pueden experimentar problemas intermitentes de acceso o retrasos en la entrega de correos electrónicos”. “Sabemos que nuestros clientes dependen de nuestros servicios para realizar trabajos importantes todos los días, y lamentamos el impacto que estos cortes tuvieron en aquellos que dependen de nosotros”, han añadido posteriormente. We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity. Según la empresa, el problema no se debe a un aumento inesperado del tráfico por mayor actividad de los usuarios, sino a que varios servidores habían dejado de estar disponibles sin que eso se esperase y su trabajo recayó sobre los que quedaban, en un efecto dominó que terminó por saturar los sistemas. No hay todavía un análisis definitivo de por qué ha pasado eso, pero lo único que parece claro es que el problema afecta a los servicios “que interactúan con Exchange Online y el correo”. Por eso arrastró a Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, asociados al correo, mientras que los que no dependen de Exchange siguen funcionando. “Lo que sabemos por ahora es que ayer hubo un aumento anormal de tráfico de red que, a priori , parece indicar un fallo técnico muy probablemente vinculado con gestión BGP y DNS [protocolos de enrutamiento de tráfico online y sistema de nombres de dominio]. No hay evidencia de ataque alguno”, explica David Arroyo Guardeño, científico titular del Grupo de Investigación en Ciberseguridad y Protección de la Privacidad (GICP) del CSIC. “Las implicaciones de esta caída son enormes en un amplio grueso de sectores industriales. Microsoft Outlook y, cada vez más Copilot, están muy presentes en un porcentaje muy amplio de nuestros servicios e infraestructura digital”, añade. Las quejas de los usuarios en la plataforma especializada Downdetector alcanzaron un primer pico pasadas las siete de la tarde del jueves, hora peninsular española, y se reportaron problemas en más de 70 países. Esta mañana, sobre las siete, ha comenzado una segunda oleada de incidencias, que ha duplicado en volumen la registrada en la tarde del jueves. Pasadas las cinco de la tarde, el nivel de incidencias se asemejaba al de un día normal. Australia amaneció este viernes con el incidente que en España se sufrió el jueves por la tarde. Ha provocado problemas en empresas, que han experimentado dificultades para comunicarse, gestionar pedidos o enviar facturas, y en organismos y servicios públicos, incluyendo la agencia tributaria australiana y algunos tribunales. La caída ha afectado también a la Policía Federal Australiana (AFP), la agencia de inteligencia ASIO y Service NSW, la plataforma del estado de Nueva Gales del Sur que permite realizar trámites como renovar permisos de conducir o gestionar matriculaciones. Por eso, las autoridades del país han activado una cláusula de su acuerdo de resiliencia digital con Microsoft para pedir que sus intereses reciban prioridad en la recuperación de los servicios afectados por la caída global de la tecnológica estadounidense. sources.title: Microsoft recupera Outlook más de 24 horas después: ya sabemos qué provocó la caída de sus servicios
sources.text: Poco más tarde de las 7 de la mañana, Microsoft 365 Status ponía punto y final a una de las caídas más largas y pronunciadas de la historia de la informática moderna. Por fin habían restaurado el servicio completamente para todos los clientes y regiones afectadas tras abordar lo que causó este incidente que ha dejado sin Outlook, Teams, Copilot y el resto de Microsoft 365 durante más de un día, ya que los fallos empezaron durante la tarde del jueves en Estados Unidos , a las 17:17 horas de España. Una caída masiva y global . El fallo se traducía en una caída global que dejó sin acceso al correo electrónico y otras herramientas profesionales de su suite, como las videollamadas o su chatbot con IA. Según Downdetector, recibió avisos de incidencias en 74 países, con un alcance que no solo no entiende de fronteras, sino tampoco de sector o tamaño: millones de empresas como la gigante Maersk en la logística , administraciones públicas como la Junta de Andalucía , así como hospitales como los del servicio nacional de salud del Reino Unido , las autoridades como en Los Angeles o hasta la prestigiosa universidad de Stanford sufrieron en sus carnes la incidencia. Por qué ha ocurrido . Horas antes de anunciar el restablecimiento completo, Microsoft se disculpaba públicamente en su perfil de y daba una explicación oficial a lo sucedido: el problema comenzó durante una actualización anterior de la capacidad de su red. Pero el fallo no apareció en ese momento, sino cuando la empresa ejecutó un cambio posterior en esa infraestructura. En el mensaje descartan además que la incidencia estuviera relacionada con la ciberseguridad o ataques IA. En cualquier caso, han prometido un informe completo del incidente al concluir la revisión. Sabíamos que el origen del fallo eran los servidores de Exchange Online, pero no por qué: primero hablaban de una "carga elevada” en varias regiones , luego de que muchos servidores se habían quedado fuera de servicio inesperadamente, más tarde apuntaban a fallos en las comprobaciones de salud automáticas , aunque esa hipótesis duró poco. Poco después, Microsoft empezó a revertir un cambio en la configuración de la red , precisamente la explicación oficial que ha dado la empresa fundada por Gates y Allen. Recuperación gradual . Una de las razones por las que la caída ha sido tan larga es cómo Microsoft ha recuperado los servicios. En el mensaje, la compañía detalla que han solucionado el problema de fondo y que han optado por un restablecimiento progresivo. Así, ha explicado que considerando la magnitud de la demanda, han ido restaurando los servicios gradualmente, validando en cada etapa que la infraestructura funcionara correctamente. Microsoft reconoce que este procedimiento ha prolongado la recuperación, pero lo ha considerado necesario para garantizar un restablecimiento estable. Cronología de la caída y la recuperación . Así ha ido evolucionando la avería de Microsoft, en hora peninsular española (CET): Pocas empresas con mucho poder . La caída pone de manifiesto hasta qué punto dependen particulares, empresas y administradores de escasos proveedores tecnológicos para tareas esenciales para su desempeño profesional. El problema no es solo no recibir un correo o no poder tener una reunión, es que cuando infraestructuras tan colosales falla, medio mundo se para: trámites administrativos que no pueden llevarse a cabo, comunicaciones internas o servicios críticos. De hecho y como recoge Reuters , hubo quien tuvo que recurrir al fax. El problema de las últimas horas es en realidad un déjá vú de la dependencia tecnológica concentrada: el fallo de ClowdStrike sobre Azure dejó a hospitales y pymes fuera de juego hace un par de años o cómo hace aproximadamente un año un fallo en AWS dejó sin internet a medio mundo . Según la Comisión Europea , Amazon con AWS, Microsoft con Azure y Google Cloud concentran más del 70% del mercado europeo. El de ayer fue una (otra) muestra más. Es que lleva tiempo equivocándose

sources.text: Roboflow helps teams meet compliance requirements and get computer vision ready for security, legal, and operations review, with documented controls: blur and pixelate blocks you can run on your own hardware to anonymize people before images leave your site, agents that ask before they act, scoped and rotatable API keys, custom roles and audit logs, and self-hosted Inference that can run fully offline. Start any review at the Roboflow Trust Center (opens in a new tab) . Computer vision projects rarely stall because a model is not accurate enough. They stall in compliance and readiness review. Security teams want to know where data lives and who can touch it. Legal teams ask about faces, consent, and biometric laws. Plant managers and labor relations teams want to know how cameras on the floor will land with the people who work there. And now that AI agents and large language models are part of the toolkit, IT teams want to know exactly what those systems can do. In this guide, we'll show how Roboflow helps you meet compliance requirements across biometrics, agent readiness, union rules and worker monitoring, using OpenAI models safely, custom governance, API keys, and local deployment. For each one, we cover what Roboflow documents today and link to the source. Below are seven areas reviewers ask about most, with the features and design patterns that address each one in Roboflow. Roboflow Workflows include built-in blocks for anonymizing people and faces: Pair a face or person detector with one of these blocks, run it on your own hardware, and the raw frame never needs to leave your site. For step by step guides, see face blurring for privacy , blurring people with an API , and how to blur a bounding box in Python . AI agents can now build datasets, train models, and assemble Workflows. That is a big productivity gain, and it raises a fair question from security teams: what exactly can an agent do, and how do we govern it? Roboflow offers four agent surfaces (opens in a new tab) : an MCP server, open source Agent Skills (opens in a new tab) , OpenAPI specs, and the in-app Roboflow Agent. Each one is built with control in mind. When you turn on Enforce Workspace LLM Keys (opens in a new tab) , every request uses your key and never falls back to Roboflow's. Features that cannot use your key are turned off, image generation is turned off, and conversation traces are not recorded. Cameras on a production floor can raise real concerns for the people who work there, and many sites operate under collective bargaining agreements or wo`rks council rules. What we offer are design patterns that keep a system focused on processes, not people: Large multimodal models such as OpenAI's GPT models are useful for describing scenes, reading text, and answering open ended questions about images. Many teams want those capabilities without sending raw images that contain faces or other sensitive details to a third party model provider. The answer is to redact first, on hardware you control, and send only the anonymized image. OpenAI models are available as a Workflows block. You can call them with a Roboflow managed key billed in credits (opens in a new tab) , or with your own key. If a workspace must never send images to an outside model, admins can use Workflows Block Governance (opens in a new tab) to disable the OpenAI block and other blocks that call external AI providers, and those changes are recorded in audit logs. Every piece of the setup below is documented. Step 1: Run Inference on Your Own Hardware Install self-hosted Inference (opens in a new tab) on a server or edge device you control. Self-hosted Inference runs Workflows locally, so the redaction step happens before any image leaves your network. Create a new Workflow and add these blocks in order: The raw camera frame. It stays on your hardware. Finds faces, people, license plates, or other sensitive regions. Blur Visualization or Pixelate Visualization Anonymizes each detected region. With a segmentation model, Blur follows the exact mask shape. Receives only the anonymized image, plus your prompt. Connect the image and the model's detections to the Blur or Pixelate block, then connect the anonymized image from that block to the OpenAI block. Only the anonymized image is passed on. Step 3: Choose Which Key Pays for the Request Pick a Roboflow managed key or your own. With Workspace LLM Keys enforced, the Workflow OpenAI and Gemini blocks and Auto Label run their OpenAI and Gemini models on your own OpenAI or Gemini key, with no fallback to Roboflow's keys, and other LLM blocks that cannot use your keys are turned off. Auto Label can also run on your own OpenAI or Gemini key (opens in a new tab) . As noted in section 2, enforcement is enabled per workspace and is not available in the EU region today. When you share a Workflow (opens in a new tab) , by default it does not run under your keys, and credentials such as an OpenAI key become inputs the other person provides. If you choose to let others run it with your hidden credentials, those credentials are redacted from any client facing data. Run a set of test images through the Workflow and review the output before you point it at a live feed. Include hard cases: faces at an angle, partly hidden, or far from the camera. To keep an anonymized copy for training, connect the Pixelate Visualization output to the Roboflow Dataset Upload block. The image that gets saved is the anonymized one. Large organizations rarely have one set of rules. Different business units, sites, and data types need different controls. Roboflow Enterprise includes tools to shape governance to your organization: API keys are often the most direct path to your data and models, so they deserve the same care as any other credential. sources.title: How to Run Computer Vision Regression Tests with Roboflow
sources.text: Catch silent accuracy drops in a vision pipeline by regression testing it with Roboflow Workflow Evals. Rerun a fixed set of test images after every model swap, retrain, or threshold change, see which images and classes got worse, and use a deploy gate to block any update that fails before it reaches production. A model update can make a pill-counting application miss objects without causing a single execution error. Changing a confidence threshold or filtering step can have the same effect. The application still returns a result, but the count your system depends on is now wrong. Computer vision regression testing helps catch these failures before deployment. You run an updated application against a fixed set of test images with reviewed answers, check its outputs, and compare the results with a baseline. You can then see where a change broke behavior that previously worked. In this guide, we’ll use Roboflow Workflow Evals (opens in a new tab) to test a Workflow that counts five types of pills. The baseline passes all 85 count checks across 17 images. After swapping one model block, that drops to 35 of 85 checks, even though the Workflow still runs successfully. We’ll walk through creating the test cases, defining correct outputs, comparing versions, and setting acceptance criteria for your next release. Computer vision regression testing checks whether a change to a vision model or application causes previously working behavior to fail. It involves rerunning a fixed set of images or videos, comparing the outputs with reviewed ground truth, and checking the results against an established baseline. Each test needs an input, an expected result, and a rule for deciding whether the output is acceptable. For a pill-counting application, the input is an image, the expected result is the correct count for each pill type, and the rule might require every count to match exactly. Run these tests after changes that could affect predictions or application logic, including model retraining, confidence threshold adjustments, preprocessing changes, and edits to filtering or counting steps. Compare versions on the same cases to find examples that newly fail. This differs from screenshot-based visual regression testing, which checks changes to a rendered user interface. Computer vision regression testing checks the predictions and decisions an application makes from visual inputs. Model evaluation (opens in a new tab) measures prediction quality using metrics such as precision, recall, and mean average precision (mAP). Repeating those measurements across model versions on the same evaluation data is one form of regression testing. Application-level regression testing extends that process to the outputs your system uses. A pill counter depends on the detector, confidence thresholds, class filters, and counting logic working together. When you evaluate the final counts, you test all of these steps together. Roboflow Workflow Evals lets you check those outputs against expected answers. In this tutorial, each pill count must match its ground truth exactly. A detector may find most pills in an image, but one missed or extra pill is enough to fail the corresponding count Check. Use model metrics to investigate prediction quality and Workflow Evals to verify that the complete application meets its output requirements. An Eval is a fixed test for a Workflow: a set of test images with known answers, plus the rules for judging what the Workflow returns. Four terms come up throughout this tutorial, so here is what each one means. Each Run records its inputs, ground truth, Workflow definitions, and settings. Editing a Case later only affects future Runs, so earlier results stay as they were. Run the Eval any time something in the Workflow changes: Because the test images and answers stay fixed, any difference between Runs comes from your change. This is the Workflow we will test, called Pill Count Per Class . It takes one image and returns five numbers, one for each pill type. The image goes to a single object detection model. Its detections then split into five branches, one per class, from pill_01 to pill_05. Each branch filters the detections down to its class, and a Property Definition block turns the result into a count. Those five counts are the Workflow’s only outputs. I set up the Workflow with the Eval in mind: every count is its own output, so each one can get its own Check, and the model sits in one block, so I can swap it without changing anything else. Both models use the same architecture, RF-DETR Small (opens in a new tab) , a real-time object detection model from Roboflow. We chose it in the training setup and changed only the training data. The baseline is trained on the train split of the pill dataset (opens in a new tab) . The dataset has 174 images, split into 122 for training, 35 for validation, and 17 for testing. The weaker model uses a 7-image version of the same data: 2 images for training, 2 for validation, and 3 for testing. I gave it far fewer examples on purpose, so it would perform worse than the baseline. The 17 Eval images are the baseline’s test split, so it has never seen them. Because neither model trained on these images, the Eval tests how each one handles images it hasn’t seen. The models themselves are only for this demo, though: for your own Workflow, retrain on your own images and validate on your own test set before relying on the results. Choose test images that represent the conditions your application needs to handle. Include everyday examples, difficult cases, and inputs where the correct answer is zero. Each should test a specific requirement of the Workflow. Review these answers carefully, and recount or remove any image with an unclear count before approving the ground truth. Keep these images and their near-duplicate

sources.title: How to Turn Videos in S3, GCS or Azure into a Computer Vision Dataset
sources.text: To label video data from S3, GCS, or Azure, connect your bucket to a Roboflow datasource and enable scheduled mirroring for MP4 and MOV files up to 3 GB each. Then use a separate frame-sampling step to prepare images, review their labels in Roboflow, and train an RF-DETR model on the resulting dataset. To label video data from S3, connect your bucket to a Roboflow datasource, mirror selected videos into your workspace, and prepare representative frames for annotation. Review the labels, create a dataset version, and train an RF-DETR model for your application. For enterprise teams, this process needs to work across cameras, locations, and changing operating conditions. A manufacturing team may need examples from several production lines; a logistics team may need footage from multiple facilities. Roboflow datasources provide a recurring connection to that footage using saved credentials, file filters, and scheduled syncing. Roboflow Datasources (opens in a new tab) adds MP4 and MOV video mirroring from AWS S3, S3-compatible storage, Google Cloud Storage, and Azure Blob Storage. Mirrored videos are stored in the Asset Library; extracting frames and preparing a labeled training dataset are separate steps covered below. Your cameras may already collect the examples your model needs. Security cameras record people moving through a warehouse. Line cameras capture products under inspection. Dashcams record changing road conditions. That footage often ends up in cloud storage, and moving it from a bucket into a labeling tool takes extra work. One minute of video at 30 frames per second contains 1,800 frames. Label every frame, and you can spend most of your time annotating almost identical views. Download a few clips once, and your dataset misses the footage that arrives tomorrow. A custom pipeline can download videos, extract frames, and upload images to a labeling tool. Keeping that pipeline running also means handling new files, retries, credentials, and duplicate imports. Adding a second cloud provider introduces another integration to maintain. Roboflow datasources handle the recurring cloud-to-workspace import. You can focus your dataset work on selecting useful scenes and labeling what the model needs to learn. A Roboflow datasource is a saved connection between your cloud storage and your Roboflow workspace. It combines a bucket or container, a reusable credential, file-selection rules, and a sync mirror configuration. With scheduling enabled, Roboflow checks for matching data daily automatically. The connection now supports videos alongside images. You can find and manage the mirrored footage in the Asset Library (opens in a new tab) , which organizes visual data across your workspace. For object detection, the next unit of training data is a labeled image. Select useful clips, extract representative frames, and create a dataset around the task you want to solve. Roboflow supports the following providers for video mirroring: These limits apply to mirroring the video files. A training dataset still requires frame selection and annotation. Split files larger than 3 GB into smaller clips before syncing them. Before connecting production footage, define which buckets and camera locations belong in the dataset, who can access the imported data, and who approves annotations before training. Use a dedicated cloud identity with read access scoped to the required bucket or container. Scope the cloud identity’s permissions to the bucket or container you need, then use file filters to choose which videos within it Roboflow imports. Within Roboflow, role-based access controls (opens in a new tab) let you separate labeling and review responsibilities. Enterprise options include custom roles and folder permissions for more specific access requirements. Audit logs (opens in a new tab) record significant workspace actions, including image approvals, dataset exports, and training activity. For datasets spanning several facilities, define a shared labeling policy and preserve source information such as site, camera, capture time, and product type. That context helps reviewers resolve ambiguous examples and helps engineers investigate differences in model performance. Start in your workspace’s Credentials settings and save access for your storage provider. Then create a Datasource . On its Connection tab, choose the provider, supply the bucket details, and select your saved credential. Use the bucket or Azure container name without a folder path. You will narrow the selection with file filters in Step 2. For an S3 video dataset, Roboflow recommends AWS Assume Role . Create an IAM role with bucket-scoped read access, and configure its trust policy using the Roboflow principal and External ID shown in the credential form. Save the role ARN in Roboflow, then select it for your datasource. IAM access keys are also supported. Follow the AWS S3 credential setup (opens in a new tab) for the required policies and credential options. For S3-compatible storage, also supply the provider’s S3 API endpoint and region. Follow the S3-compatible configuration instructions (opens in a new tab) for endpoint and addressing requirements. stories.title: Roboflow Serverless vs. Self-Hosted Inference: What a 90-Second Traffic Spike Does to One GPU Server
stories.summary: Sizing GPUs for the traffic you expect works until traffic does something you didn’t expect. In our load test, a short burst left one GPU server timing out even after traffic returned to normal, while Roboflow Serverless kept up. Here’s what went wrong, and why autoscaling can’t add a GPU in time.
